title: SIR row: Will annul EC orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
content: The Supreme Court has asked the Election Commission to clarify decision-making processes related to voter roll revisions. It emphasized that decisions should be taken unanimously or by majority among commission members only. Senior advocate Vikas Singh argued for preserving records and scrutiny of the commission's actions. The court will examine allegations of unilateral actions against the Chief Election Commissioner.

title: 86 to 101: Kohli's final ODI window to break Tendulkar's century record
content: Virat Kohli is 15 centuries away from becoming the first batter to reach 101 international hundreds, with ODI cricket now his only route to Sachin Tendulkar's record. India have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the 2027 World Cup, while the Asia Cup offers additional opportunities. A possible six-match South Africa series in the new FTP could give India further preparation before the World Cup, but the century chase remains a difficult one.

title: Before triple murder, Bengaluru techie used AI to ‘rehearse’ attack scenarios
content: In a shocking incident in Seegehalli, Bengaluru, techie J Kenneth allegedly murdered his partner's family. He had used artificial intelligence to research various methods of attack prior to the crime. Shwetha, Kenneth's partner, had borrowed substantial loans to support him, causing family tension. Following a confrontation with her parents about the loans, Kenneth reportedly carried out the violent act. Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic event.

title: Accenture CEO rejects concerns that AI is a threat to the company’s business model
content: Accenture's CEO Julie Sweet shared insights on significant advancements in artificial intelligence impacting the company. Over 400 clients have started advanced AI projects in the past fiscal year. The company recorded fourth-quarter revenue growth fueled by AI-driven efficiencies and client transformation integration. Additionally, productivity enhancements have allowed for executing larger projects without proportional headcount increases. Accenture intends to moderate recruitment rates as automation continues to absorb operational tasks.

title: Woman declares Rs 67.4L ancestral jewellery in ITR; gets notice, she wins in ITAT
content: The assessment threw up two separate issues. The first concerned jewellery worth Rs 67,39,949 that the woman had disclosed in Schedule AL of her income tax return. The tribunal also examined whether the Rs 12 lakh paid to the HUF represented a genuine brokerage expense when the same person, the HUF's Karta/coparcener, had already received another Rs 12 lakh for the same transaction.

title: In Japan, women’s sumo battles tradition and a male-dominated system for survival
content: More than 100 women gathered at the Kyoto City Budo Centre to practice sumo wrestling. Despite historic resistance, female participation in sumo is increasing, with over 600 women involved in various clubs. The Japan Sumo Association does not recognise women's sumo, leaving many to rely on private clubs for training. Coaches and athletes express hope for future Olympic inclusion as they work to build awareness.

title: Houthis target Aramco refinery, Saudi capital airport as Mecca defence pact activated
content: Yemen's Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia's infrastructure. The reported strikes included key sites such as airports and an Aramco refinery. In response, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces have intensified their offensive against the Houthis along the Red Sea coast. The conflict has prompted Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye to activate their defense pact for collective response.

title: Oil prices hover near $100 as Middle East supply holds up, Gulf risks persist
content: Oil prices are currently around $100 a barrel as stable Middle Eastern exports ease supply concerns. However, ongoing regional conflicts, including Houthi attacks, raise risks of disruptions. Officials indicate that rebuilding global oil stockpiles could take years due to significant withdrawals. Industry executives predict that demand recovery may not occur until 2028 or 2029. Prices may stabilize at around $70 a barrel depending on future production levels.

title: China's desert oilfield hits record: 8,080m deep core from 500m-year-old rock
content: China’s Fuman Oilfield in Xinjiang has extracted 26.86 million tons of oil and gas equivalent from ultra-deep formations beneath the Taklimakan Desert. Engineers also recovered rock cores from a record depth of 8,080 metres at the Zhentan-1 well. The rocks are estimated to have remained buried for about 500 million years, according to CNPC and CCTV.

title: England's lost Atlantis Shipden found beneath North Sea after 700 years
content: Divers surveying the seabed off Cromer, Norfolk, have mapped 25 manmade structures linked to Shipden, a medieval village swallowed by the North Sea centuries ago. The underwater search is also challenging the long-held belief that Church Rock marks St Peter’s Church, as researchers investigate new evidence about the vanished settlement and changing coastline.

title: In 2009, Google’s Eric Schmidt bought a ship; by 2022, it mapped 1.3m sq km of seafloor
content: In 2009, Eric and Wendy Schmidt took a significant step in marine conservation by acquiring a fisheries protection vessel, rebranding it as Falkor. This vessel became a hub for oceanographic research and exploration, hosting over 1,000 scientists and charting more than 1.3 million square kilometers of the ocean by 2022.

title: Why kids keep touching your face while talking, per psychology
content: Children frequently display physical affection towards their parents, such as gently touching their faces while talking. This interaction not only nurtures a sense of closeness but also helps them assess their parents' engagement. Studies indicate that such affectionate gestures are crucial for emotional growth throughout childhood. Parents must recognize the importance of these moments while also upholding appropriate boundaries to enhance emotional safety and deepen the parent-child relationship.

title: Trump signs order to ease diesel costs, ‘save millions of dollars’ for farmers
content: In response to rising diesel prices, US President Donald Trump has enacted an executive order designed to alleviate financial pressures across multiple sectors. This order is anticipated to substantially cut fuel costs for farmers and truck drivers, ultimately contributing to lower grocery prices. Additionally, it urges states to expand access to tax-free red-dyed diesel and consider lifting specific fuel taxes.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m mansion: Why does it have a $1.75m twin in Illinois?
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion, Moyenage, has a fascinating architectural connection to a $1.75 million home in Wheaton, Illinois. Both properties were designed by architect Jarvis Hunt for steel magnate Jay C. Morse, with the Ohio estate reportedly based on his earlier Illinois residence. The 10,000-square-foot House of Seven Gables retains historic details, including fireplaces, oak panelling, beamed ceilings and carved woodwork, despite being relocated in 2017.

title: Naomi Osaka’s family mission: How did her Haitian roots inspire her work?
content: Naomi Osaka's heartfelt bond with Haiti is rooted in her family's foundation, which was formed in 1999 to uplift the community. Her inaugural trip to Haiti occurred in October 2017, followed by another visit after her first Grand Slam win in 2018. Engaging with local children, she championed educational initiatives and allocated part of her earnings for earthquake relief. This connection deeply influences Osaka's ongoing philanthropic endeavors.

title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
content: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations.

title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
content: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.

title: Missed IIT by 0.01, rejected by MIT: Meet Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas
content: Aravind Srinivas overcame significant educational hurdles after failing to meet the cut-off at IIT Madras. Taking charge of his learning, he self-taught programming and excelled in competitive challenges. Following successful internships at top AI research facilities, he co-founded Perplexity AI in 2022. Now, at just a young age, he boasts a remarkable net worth of $2.1 billion, showcasing his unwavering resilience and hard work.

title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
content: BJP has chosen not to renominate Union ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma for Rajya Sabha. This decision raises speculation about a possible reshuffle of the council of ministers by PM Narendra Modi. Since several ministers have been given organization roles, it indicates their continuation in government may be unlikely. Puri's term ends in November, and he may be reassigned for the Punjab assembly polls.

title: 'We all have huge sympathy': Why England cricket ready to fund West Indies Test
content: The ECB could provide financial support to Cricket West Indies to ensure England’s women play a Test in the Caribbean next spring. The match is viewed as vital preparation for the 2027 Ashes, with England seeking more red-ball cricket. Despite CWI’s financial difficulties and recent cost-cutting measures, the Test and wider multi-format tour remain on schedule.

title: Delhi Police ACP's additional DCP charge withheld amid harassment inquiry
content: Delhi government modified an order regarding duty charges of 12 police officers after harassment allegations surfaced. Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat voluntarily stepped aside from his additional charge as the inquiry continues. The CDC assignment began prior to the allegations, ensuring it does not indicate a promotion. The complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a detailed investigation and fair inquiry.

title: Proposed GST changes positive for business: Experts
content: Proposed changes to the GST regime are expected to benefit businesses, improving cash flow and refunds. A refund on accumulated GST for input services and capital goods may help manufacturers significantly. The GST Council will discuss the rationalization of ITC, which has long been an issue for businesses. Decriminalization of certain GST provisions aims to create a more business-friendly environment in India.

title: Before UPSC interview, father fixes son’s coat, combs his hair; video wins hearts
content: In a touching video, a father is seen preparing his son for an upcoming interview at the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission. He adjusts the boy’s coat, styles his hair, and hands him sweets for luck. Viewers on social media connected deeply with this display of a supportive father-son relationship, sharing personal anecdotes of similar nurturing moments they’ve had before important life events.

title: India-US trade talks have reached plateau: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
content: Negotiations regarding the bilateral trade agreement between India and the US have stalled, reaching a plateau. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that both sides face difficulties in making further concessions. The US aims to reduce its trade imbalance with India, while recent laws have complicated matters. Discussions included tariffs impacting agricultural imports and energy purchases from the US.

title: Drishyam 3 dips on Day 4, crosses Rs 300 crore worldwide
content: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion has achieved over Rs 300 crore in worldwide gross collections shortly after its release. Following a strong opening weekend, the film saw a significant drop in earnings on Monday. Its total net collection in India reached Rs 197.50 crore, while overseas collections contributed an additional Rs 66 crore. The film recorded nearly 8 million footfalls across India within the first four days of its release.

title: Kheri case: UP changes PP; SC asks Allahabad HC CJ to decide on trial judge
content: The Uttar Pradesh government informed the Supreme Court about replacing the public prosecutor in the Lakhimpur Kheri case. This decision was made in response to allegations raised against the outgoing prosecutor by a witness involved in the case. As the Supreme Court monitors the trial's progress, it was noted that 86 witnesses have been examined thus far.

title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
content: The National Household Travel Survey indicates that only 15% of workers use public transport for commuting. It reveals that 46% of workers rely on two-wheelers and cars, leading to traffic congestion. Walking is the second most common commute mode, with 28.3% of workers traveling on foot. Student commuting patterns differ significantly, with 37% walking to educational institutions.

title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced
content: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced achieved a record high in 2026 while their IIT seat share remained mostly unchanged. A total of 10,107 women qualified, reflecting a 7.5% increase in their qualifying count. Admissions across IITs reached 18,861, with 20% allocated to female candidates. Significant gains were reported for SC and ST candidates in qualification rates.

title: Mission Shakti: How India’s 2019 anti-sat missile test in space caught US off guard
content: India conducted an unexpected anti-satellite missile test in 2019, which surprised US security agencies completely. The former NRO officer David Grusch recounted his experiences during the incident on a podcast. India announced its capability after destroying a defunct satellite, making it the fourth country to achieve such technology. This test led to concerns about debris affecting US satellites in orbit.

title: India, Switzerland eye deeper ties in trade, investment, tech
content: India and Switzerland have signed five agreements to strengthen cooperation in trade and mobility. The two countries aim to enhance market access for Indian exports and attract Swiss investments in key sectors. A new mobility agreement will facilitate easier access for Indian professionals and students to Switzerland. Both leaders discussed global conflicts and emphasized the importance of dialogue for peace.

title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
content: The Supreme Court initially planned an informal meeting with the parliamentary committee on simultaneous elections. However, the meeting was canceled after opposition MPs raised concerns about the appropriateness of the interaction. The Supreme Court expressed that discussing the matter could lead to future judicial review. The proposal for the meeting was suggested by DMK MP P Wilson.

title: Pahalgam handler rallies LeT support via anti-Israel rhetoric
content: Saifullah Kasuri made controversial remarks regarding the Pakistan army's role in regional conflicts. He threatened to erase Israel from the world map and defend Saudi holy sites. After the Pahalgam attack, he has been active in public events to raise support. High-level meetings between Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hamas have been reported, indicating growing connections. Kasuri's actions reflect an increasing boldness post-attack, as he recruits youth and gathers funds.

title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
content: The Delhi High Court emphasized that foreign nationals do not have an inherent right to enter India. Justice Amit Mahajan pointed out that holding a visa does not ensure unconditional admission. The court noted various factors that could lead to denial of entry, including national security and public health. A plea by a Turkmenistan woman for reasons regarding her entry refusal was dismissed.

title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
content: Nearly 23 years after the Tamil Nadu assembly's breach of privilege resolution, a Supreme Court hearing is scheduled. The resolution imposed a 15-day sentence on some journalists but has since been withdrawn. Senior advocates claimed that the writ petition's cause of action no longer exists and argued the matter has become academic. As a result, the Supreme Court is expected to dispose of the petitions.

title: World entering age of flux, India will rise to challenges: EAM S Jaishankar
content: S Jaishankar emphasized the uncertainties facing the world during his speech at the Kautilya Economic Conclave. He expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate challenges such as conflicts and economic volatility. The minister highlighted India's proactive stance during crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Jaishankar called for diplomacy to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, particularly concerning maritime security.

title: Not now daal-ing, says MAGA, as Montana governor comes to India to sell pulses
content: Montana's Governor Greg Gianforte is heading a delegation to India to promote agricultural exports. The focus is on selling lentils, peas, and chickpeas to the world's largest consumer of pulses. This trip highlights the growing tension within the Republican party regarding international trade and immigration. Many in the GOP criticize Gianforte's outreach to India amidst concerns about jobs for Americans.

title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
content: A Russian drone struck the MV Royad Mammadov cargo vessel in the Black Sea, resulting in two fatalities. Among the crew were three Indian nationals, one of whom sustained injuries and received medical care. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy confirmed that the ship's captain was killed in the attack and expressed condolences. Romanian authorities responded to the incident by rescuing 11 crew members and recovering two deceased individuals.

title: Rawat seeks meet with Congress brass as Kumari Selja slams his yatra plan
content: Harish Rawat's thanksgiving yatra has prompted a strong response from AICC, emphasizing the need for party unity. Kumari Selja has criticized the yatra as a parallel program that undermines Congress interests. The party leadership has expressed concern regarding Rawat's controversial statements and the potential division of support. A meeting between Rawat and Selja is expected to take place later this week.

title: Supreme Court may get 3 judges today, to be one short of full strength
content: The Union law ministry has announced the appointment of three judges to the Supreme Court. Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh have been elevated. These judges were previously chief justices of their respective high courts and will be sworn in soon. With these appointments, the Supreme Court remains one judge short of its sanctioned strength.

title: Form 6 not modified, only declaration added: Election Commission
content: Election Commission officials clarified that there was no change to Form 6, only an additional declaration form was introduced. This statement followed CJI Surya Kant's observation regarding the approval of modified Form 6. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Chief Election Commissioner of making illegal changes to the form. The Election Commission denied these accusations and referred to a previous press note for clarification.

title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Azad, court directs Delhi cops
content: A Delhi court has ordered the completion of an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Chandrashekhar Azad. The complainant accused Azad of raping her under the pretext of marriage and claimed the police did not register an FIR. The police sought additional time for the inquiry, but the complainant opposed this request. The court rejected the police's plea and emphasized that the alleged offence is punishable with life imprisonment.

title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
content: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan raised concerns regarding the deletion of voters through special intensive revision, facing criticism from former CJI BR Gavai. While Bhuyan emphasized that disenfranchising citizens violates constitutional rights, Gavai expressed reservations about commenting on ongoing legal matters. Former Supreme Court judge Rohinton Fali Nariman also voiced concerns about the democratic implications of voters being removed from lists.

title: NCW issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based transport services
content: The National Commission for Women has released guidelines aimed at improving safety for women passengers using app-based transport services. These measures include verifying the background of drivers and ensuring proper identification matches. Additionally, the guidelines address issues related to late-night travel and unauthorized changes in drivers or vehicles. Aggregators are encouraged to create a verified pool of women drivers to enhance safety.

title: Pretty in pink, but Malarikkal’s lilies worry ecologists
content: A two-year study for the Kerala State Biodiversity Board finds the water lily, which appeared in Malarikkal after the 2018 floods, has shown unprecedented and uncontrolled growth; ecologists flag its impact on local aquatic plants, water flow and sunlight penetration, besides concerns over methane emissions from decaying plant biomass; the seasonal bloom has transformed Malarikkal into a tourism hotspot, bringing additional income to farmers, boat operators and local residents

content: Circular had permitted corrections in title deed forms where survey numbers were erroneously entered. Survey numbers were amended in over 600 cases by misusing the circular, according to the Land Revenue Commissioner’s communication to the government sent in August 2026

content: This is the first batch of cargo to be shipped from upper Assam's Dibrugarh to a foreign port since India's independence in 1947. The event comes nearly 70 years after the town's river ghat closed.

content: Polling is being held in Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal, Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu. Puducherry's Thattanchavady and Assam's the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency are also due for polls.

content: Brahmadathan was killed by lightning on Sunday evening. He had been tethered near the house of his owner, Advocate Rajesh Pallattu, president of the Kerala Festival Coordination Committee.

title: 600 Illegal Bangladeshi Immigrants Identified In J&K, 150 Deported
content: On Monday, a batch of 150 people was flown on a special Indian Air Force plane to Bagdogra, where they were handed over to Border Security Force (BSF) personnel, the officials said.

title: Trump Says He Will Pay For Political Ads After Row Over Taxpayer Funding
content: The White House and Trump had vigorously defended the ads as simply patriotic public service announcements similar to ones done by previous presidents. But they still elicited criticism from both parties.

title: Germany At Risk Of "Violent Conflict" With Russia, Claims Spy Chief
content: German authorities have warned repeatedly that Russia is conducting a hybrid campaign of drone and cyber attacks, accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport in August.

title: Jeffrey Archer, UK Author And Former Conservative Politician, Dies At 86
content: British author Jeffrey Archer, who penned a series of best-selling novels, served as a Conservative MP and was convicted of perjury, died suddenly at 86, his publisher HarperCollins said.

title: Woman, 26, Jumps Into Well With 4-Year-Old Son In UP, Both Die: Cops
content: A 26-year-old woman allegedly jumped into a well along with her four-year-old son on Monday, with police saying they have retrieved both bodies while the reasons behind the extreme step remain unknown.

title: Iran-Backed Houthis Say They Attacked Riyadh Airport, Aramco Refinery
content: The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen said Monday they had struck the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, an Aramco refinery and sites across the kingdom's south.

title: Trump Offers Help To Russia After Suspected Plague Death, Quarantines
content: A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people.

title: Trump Says US Moved All B-1 Bombers From UK Airbase After "Some Threats"
content: Washington confirmed earlier that the bombers had left the RAF Fairford airbase -- used by the United States to launch strikes on Tehran -- even as the British government insisted the site was safe.

title: For First Time, Pakistan To Deploy Troops To Aide Saudi-Backed Yemen Forces
content: Turkey and Pakistan will undertake a "rapid deployment" of troops to Saudi Arabia as part of a new mutual defence alliance, the three countries said Monday, as the Gulf kingdom faces escalating attacks from Yemen's Houthis.

title: "Rohan" Carved On Minor's Chest: Indian Man Behind Global Paedophile Ring
content: The case first came into light in 2020, as part of an initiative by the US National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children to combat child sexual abuse. The organisation discovered online images of a 12-year-old girl with her chest exposed.
